extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing grant proposals and performing molecular microbiology experiments (S. aureus gene regulation)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed experimental design and rationale for Specific Aims investigating SarA function in S. aureus, including controls, assays (Western, EMSA, footprinting, reporter), data interpretation, and contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describes rationale for approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes rationale for approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why specific strains, assays, and comparisons are chosen; refer to preliminary data to justify experimental choices and to explain inclusion/exclusion of reagents or strains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group experiments by experimental question
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments are grouped by experimental question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure aims/parts so each experimental cluster addresses a defined question (e.g., temporal accumulation, DNA‑binding activity, transcriptional activation). This clarifies logic and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide extensive methodological detail for procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Application includes extensive details on how they will proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give step-by-step methods (growth conditions, harvest times, buffer compositions, incubation times, centrifugation speeds, assay conditions) so reviewers can assess feasibility and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference well-established methods rather than repeat full protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-established methods are referenced, not described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite standard protocols when appropriate and only provide full details for novel or modified methods; this saves space while demonstrating familiarity with standard techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate negative and background controls
rubrics_metrics.description: These strains carry transposon insertions in the sarA structural gene and are included as negative controls for their respective parent strains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include mutant and parent strain controls, promoter-less reporter vectors, and pre-immune serum or other negative antibody controls to establish baseline/background signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify inclusion of specific strains or mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: Its inclusion is based on the hypothesis that RNAIII may contribute to the production of SarA... inclusion of RN6911 is warranted because 1) the impact of agr on sar has not been examined beyond Northern blots and 2) RNAIII is known to affect at least one protein post-transcriptionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain alternative mechanistic rationales and why a particular mutant is needed to test them (e.g., to probe post-transcriptional vs transcriptional effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define time points and verify growth phase experimentally
rubrics_metrics.description: Cells will be harvested after 2, 4, 6 and 8 hours of growth... assumptions about growth phase will be verified by monitoring the optical density of each culture at 560 nm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select sampling times based on preliminary data and verify phase transitions (e.g., OD measurements) rather than assuming timing; justify choice relative to transcript/protein production peaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure genetic insert stability without selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the mutations ... involve chromosomal insertions, all cultures will be grown without antibiotic selection. However, to ensure the stability of each insertion, duplicate plate counts utilizing medium with and without antibiotics will be done at the completion of each experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If growing without selection, include checks (e.g., plate counts on selective vs non-selective medium) to confirm insert retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish assay sensitivity and adjust protocol or scale accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the appropriate dilution of the anti-SarA antibody ... If the sensitivity of the assay is sufficient (estimated at ~10 ng of purified SarA), subsequent Western blots will be done using the same dilution of antibody. If the detection limit is >10 ng, then we will decrease the antibody dilution or scale up lysate production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically determine detection limits (titration with purified antigen), choose antibody dilution that yields reproducible signal with minimal background, and have contingency plans (increase antibody or sample amount).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pre-immune serum / IgG as background control for antibody-based assays
rubrics_metrics.description: The sensitivity of the Western blot protocol will be confirmed by repetitive blots using IgG purified from pre-immune serum ... The dilution of the SarA antibody to be used ... will be the concentration ... without a background signal with the same dilution of pre-immune serum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare signal to pre-immune IgG at same dilution to ensure specificity and determine working dilution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct standard curves for quantitative densitometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the appropriate dilution is determined, a standard curve will be constructed based on the densitometric analysis of Western blot radiographs. The amount of SarA in each cell lysate will be determined by comparison to this standard curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use known amounts of purified protein to generate a standard curve for converting densitometric signal to absolute or relative protein amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlate protein amount with transcript levels and activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of SarA in lysates prepared from each strain at different time points will be correlated with the production of individual sar transcripts in the same strains at the same time points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure transcript levels (e.g., Northern blot) and functional activity (e.g., EMSA, reporter assays) in the same time-course samples to connect expression with activity and mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design EMSA DNA concentration relative to KD (use 100x KD for whole-cell lysates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of DNA used in EMSA experiments with whole cell lysates will be 100-fold higher than the KD determined using purified SarA... Under those conditions, stoichiometric binding occurs such that the concentration of protein required to bind 50% of the available DNA (P1/2) is equal to 50% of the input DNA concentration [DNAo].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine KD with purified protein and then choose DNA input (e.g., 100× KD) so P1/2 approximates half the DNA concentration; this enables estimation of protein concentration from bound fraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specificity controls in EMSA (supershift and competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specificity of the protein-DNA complex observed by EMSA will be confirmed by supershift with anti-SarA antibody and by competition experiments employing unlabeled DNAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm identities of shifted bands by supershift with specific antibody and by competition with unlabeled specific and nonspecific DNA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report binding activity as ratio total_protein / bound_protein to infer post-translational effects
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether the DNA-binding activity of SarA is a direct function of the concentration of SarA in the cell, the results will be reported as the ratio of the total amount of SarA as defined by Western blot versus the amount of SarA bound to each DNA target ... any decrease will be taken as an indication that the DNA-binding activity of SarA can be affected by post-translational modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare total protein quantity to DNA‑binding competent fraction; changes in this ratio across conditions indicate changes in activity per molecule (e.g., modifications, cofactors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reporter fusions with promoter-less controls
rubrics_metrics.description: These experiments will be done using derivatives ... carrying either a P2-xylE reporter fusion or a P3-xylE reporter fusion. Variants of each strain that contain the promoter-less xylE vector will be included as negative controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include promoter-less reporter vectors as negative controls and use appropriate antibiotic selection markers for plasmid maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtract background reporter activity measured in mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure that the results reflect the functional activity of SarA, the CATase activity observed when the xylE fusions ... are introduced into the Sar R and 11D2 mutants will be taken as the background CATase activity associated with each of the parent strains. The background activity observed with each mutant will be subtracted from the results obtained with the corresponding parent strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and subtract strain-specific background reporter activity (e.g., due to plasmid, vector, or endogenous factors) to isolate SarA-dependent signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret activity vs protein abundance to infer alternative functional forms
rubrics_metrics.description: If the activity of SarA as a transcriptional activator is dependent only on the production of SarA, then changes in CATase activity as a function of growth phase should be consistent with changes in the amount of SarA. An increase in CATase activity without a corresponding increase in the concentration of SarA will be taken as an indication that SarA exists in alternative forms that differ in their ability to activate transcription.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discordance between abundance and activity to hypothesize post-translational modification, isoforms, or cofactors; design follow-up experiments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementation analysis to identify required transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of the specific sar transcripts required to restore the sar-mediated regulation of cna transcription ... will be done by introducing plasmids encoding each sar transcript into a cna-positive sar mutant and assessing the effect on cna transcription.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plasmid-borne constructs that express overlapping transcripts to map functional regions; correlate complementation with transcript production, binding activity, and phenotype (e.g., collagen binding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localize binding sites by EMSA with progressively smaller fragments and competition
rubrics_metrics.description: To further localize the SarA-binding site(s) upstream of cna, we will synthesize DNA fragments corresponding to progressively smaller regions ... EMSA experiments will be done ... It is anticipated that these experiments will allow us to localize the SarA-binding site to a region spanning 50-100 bp. All fragments that are bound by SarA will be used in 'mix and match' competition experiments aimed at defining the relative affinity of SarA for different binding sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map binding regions by narrowing fragments, then use competition assays to rank affinities and prioritize fragments for footprinting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map protected bases by DNase I footprinting and methylation interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the smallest DNA fragment(s) bound by SarA have been identified, the same fragment(s) will be characterized by DNase I footprinting and methylation interference assays ... DNase I footprinting will allow us to define the region containing the SarA-binding site and the methylation interference assays will provide an indication of the relative significance of specific guanine and adenine residues within the protected region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use footprinting to define protected stretches and methylation interference to identify critical bases; include appropriate controls (no-enzyme lanes, free DNA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define sequence specificity by systematic mutagenesis and EMSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Once we have identified the protected region ... we will generate sequence variants by synthesizing complementary pairs of oligonucleotides that span the protected region ... design oligonucleotides to introduce specific nucleotide substitutions ... evaluate by EMSA at various SarA concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted base substitutions informed by methylation interference to create variants; test binding at multiple protein concentrations and confirm specificity by competition assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate functional significance in vivo using reporter assays and ratio metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The functional significance of the putative SarA-binding site(s) will be assessed by in vivo experiments in which different versions of the cna target(s) are cloned into the xylE reporter gene vector ... The results will be evaluated by comparison to the wild-type promoter region and will be reported as the ratio of CATase activity observed with each variant versus the activity observed with the wild-type sequence (CATase activity of variant/CATase activity of wild-type). Because mutation of sar results in overexpression of cna, elimination of the SarA binding site should result in increased xylE expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report variant activity relative to wild-type; choose a restricted, informative subset of variants (those that retain binding and those that lose binding) for in vivo tests to demonstrate functional relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use existing core facilities and preliminary reagent access to streamline methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Molecular Biology Core Facility at the PI’s institution ... includes an oligonucleotide synthesizer that can be used to generate as many sequence variants as necessary. Since they developed and had access to reagents in preliminary studies, they don’t need to state how they will obtain them here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage institutional cores and previously developed reagents; when reagents/techniques are already established in preliminary work, brief justification suffices rather than detailed procurement plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide alternatives and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives are provided to accommodate different results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe alternative approaches if initial assays lack sensitivity or produce unexpected results (e.g., change antibody dilution, scale up lysates, use alternative assays). Contingency planning strengthens feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design PCR-assisted binding site selection (PCR-ABS) with flanking unique primer sites and randomized central region
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesis of the appropriate pool of DNAs is accomplished by synthesizing three oligonucleotides ... One of these will be a 70-mer that includes defined 20 bp sites at each end. The only requirements for the design of these defined sites are 1) that they have no obvious similarity to the binding site of interest and 2) that they are distinct by comparison to each other. ... The sequence of the 30 bp region between the 20 bp sites is irrelevant ... amplification is done using an equimolar mixture of all four nucleotides such that the 30 bp region between the primer sites has a random sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For selection experiments use unique flanking primer sites lacking similarity to candidate binding motifs and avoid primer self-annealing; randomize internal region by equimolar nucleotide synthesis; plan primers accordingly for PCR amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize fragments/sites based on affinity (lowest SarA concentration yielding a shift)
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiments described below will be done starting with the DNA fragments that exhibit the highest affinity for SarA (i.e. that exhibit a gel shift with the lowest concentration of SarA and are not competitively inhibited in the presence of other, unlabeled DNA fragments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank candidate sites by apparent affinity in EMSA and focus mapping and functional assays on highest-affinity targets first.
